name: 広東料理 鳳泉 (Kanton Ryori Hosen)

claims.text: The signature dish is wheat Chinese noodles tossed in mustard-soy sauce under a chicken/kombu broth an; spring rolls, shumai and fried rice are cooked in shared woks — gluten is pervasive throughout the menu.
The karashi-soba is dressed in カラシ醤油 (mustard soy sauce); standard Japanese/Chinese soy sauce is wheat-based.
Broths are made from chicken bone and kombu, and the signature noodle is shrimp-and-chicken (エビカシワソバ); no plant-only preparations indicated.

The kitchen will adjust the amount of mustard to order, including making the dish with no mustard at all — showing willingness to customize, though this is a seasoning preference and not an allergen-handling policy.

The spicy tare and seasoning are built on a minced-meat, garlic and scallion base typical of Japanese spicy noodles, which generally relies on wheat-containing soy/seasoning; no wheat-free tare is advertised.
All noodle and broth preparations share a kitchen centered on pork cartilage, minced meat and egg, so cross-contact with animal products is unavoidable.
Shoyu-based ramen tare at Japanese ramen shops is normally made with wheat-containing soy sauce, and the noodles are wheat; no gluten-free preparation is indicated here.
Broths and toppings are animal-based (duck, fish niboshi, pork, chicken); no separate vegan preparation is noted.

name: 京・清水 油そば ねこまた (Kyo-Kiyomizu Abura Soba Nekomata)

claims.text: Wheat-based abura soba noodles and a soy (wheat) tare are the core of every bowl; no gluten-free preparation is offered or mentioned.
The dish is built on a soy-based (shoyu) tare, which in standard Japanese practice contains wheat.
Bowls include diced chashu pork plus naruto fish cake and menma; no vegan/vegetarian version is described.

name: 京ラーメン さだかず (Kyo Ramen Sadakazu)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in shared water; the dish is built on a wheat-containing soy-sauce tare. No gluten-free handling is mentioned anywhere.
The broth is a soy-sauce (shoyu) base, which in standard Japanese ramen contains wheat-fermented soy sauce; no wheat-free tare is indicated.
Broth is chicken-bone based and finished with pork back-fat and chashu pork; there is no separate vegan preparation.

name: 京都金閣寺 らーめんなか澤 (Kyoto Kinkakuji Ramen Nakasawa)

claims.text: Bowls are dressed with a three-year-aged soy-sauce (shoyu) tare; soy sauce of this type is wheat-based, making the shoyu bowls unsuitable for gluten-free diners.
The single shared broth is an animal stock (chicken, pork, clam, fish); there is no separate vegetarian or vegan preparation, so no bowl can be made vegan.

name: 京都北山元町らーめん (Kyoto Kitayama Motomachi Ramen)

claims.text: The broth is seasoned with a tamari-style soy sauce tare, which is a wheat-based fermented seasoning.

name: 京都二条 麺屋 啜る (Kyoto Nijo Menya Susuru)

claims.text: 中華麺（小麦）と熟成醤油のかえしが基本で、グルテンフリー麺や専用調理ラインの記載は確認できない。小麦の交差接触は避けられないと考えるのが安全。
看板メニューは『熟成醤油』のかえしを用いる。一般的な醸造醤油は小麦を含むため、醤油由来の小麦混入を前提に判断するのが妥当。
『ヴィーガン白湯』『ヴィーガン担々』は動物性不使用をうたう専用メニューだが、同一厨房で鶏清湯・煮干し・A5和牛・豚餃子などを調理しており、麺の茹で湯や調理器具の共用、交差接触の管理についての明記はない。
豆乳と香味野菜でつくる動物性不使用のヴィーガン白湯らぁ麺（トッピングはがんもどき・赤水菜）と、ヴィーガン担々らぁ麺を常設しており、プラントベースの一杯を注文できる。
